text:
maya: Heads up — infra CI is intermittently failing on `terraform init` in the gpu-nodepool repo. Started ~ 30m ago, ~40% flakes on main branch runs.
sam: Can you paste the error?
maya: Sure — snippet from the failing job:
```
Error: Failed to query available provider packages
caused by: Error while downloading provider: Get "https://releases.hashicorp.com/registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/google/4.65.0: net/http: TLS handshake timeout"
```
maya: Also saw `lookup registry.terraform.io: no such host` in a few runs.
devops-bot: [CI] gpu-nodepool / main #452 failed — terraform-init (runner-17) <https://ci.redwood.example/runs/452|view run> :rotating_light:
lee: Huh. This looks like transient DNS or rate-limiting to the provider registry. We had a spike in concurrent CI runs yesterday. Could be connection exhaustion from GH hosted runners.
anya: We changed the infra workflows to parallelize per-region applies last week; might be correlated.
sam: Are these GH-hosted runners or our self-hosted fleet?
maya: GH-hosted for this repo — we only use self-hosted for heavy provisioning.
lee: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) cache provider binaries (TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR + actions/cache), 2) add retry wrapper around `terraform init` to absorb transient network issues.
maya: +1 on caching. I can open a PR to add `actions/cache@v4` for `~/.terraform.d/plugins` but worried about differing OS/arch combos.
anya: We only run linux/x86_64 in these workflows, so cache key can include OS and provider version.
sam: For retries, simplest is a tiny shell wrapper:
```
for i in 1 2 3; do terraform init && break || sleep $((i*10)); done
```
This has saved us before.
lee: Also consider setting `TF_REGISTRY_CLIENT_TIMEOUT` (not official but we can set env proxy settings) and bumping git action step timeout.
maya: There's another hypothesis: some runs show `tls: certificate signed by unknown authority` when the job pulls from an internal mirror we started experimenting with. Could be intermittent CA chain problem with that mirror.
runner-bot: Automatic note: runner-17 reported short-lived network outage at 2026-03-17T11:14:02Z, packet loss to 13.225.96.0/19 (gh provider registry) for ~22s.
anya: If there's intermittent packet loss, retries + caching are both necessary. Also let's gate region parallelism so we don't bulldoze the registry with spikes.
sam: Agreed. Proposed short-term plan: (1) Add actions/cache for `~/.terraform.d/plugin-cache` keyed by provider versions and workflow hash. (2) Wrap `terraform init` with 3 retries and exponential backoff. (3) Add a concurrency lock per-repo to reduce simultaneous inits (use `concurrency: "init-${{ github.ref }}"`).
maya: I'll draft the PR with 1+2 today. Can we also add a health check job that just does `curl -I https://registry.terraform.io` before heavy steps?
lee: Health check is fine as a preflight; fail fast and mark as retriable.
devops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-873: "CI: terraform init flakes — provider registry timeouts" and assigned to @maya. <https://tracker.redwood.example/INFRA-873|view ticket>.
anya: Long-term we should mirror providers on our artifact proxy (artifactory/s3) for critical repos or adopt private provider registry caching.
sam: Also log the exact `TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` layout in the repo docs so self-hosted and GH-hosted share the same expectations.
maya: Will do. One more gotcha: pinned provider versions will help determinism but might increase cache churn when we update. We'll pin major.minor and update quarterly.
lee: OK. After the PR lands we'll run 20 canary runs on main with the cache and retry enabled, then roll to other repos if stable.
maya: PR opened: https://git.redwood.example/infra-ci/pulls/212 / includes cache + retry + quick `curl` preflight. Please review. :pray:
sam: Reviewing now. If green, let's merge and monitor CI failure rate.
anya: Thanks — awesome triage. :thumbsup:
